**Working through the consequences**

The critical rule is that the Ashcombe Design Registry will only accept a filing made *before* public showing, and a design shown first is refused and cannot be filed again. This is exactly what happened with Saltmarrow.

Tidewrack's warp comes off the loom on 2026-10-20, and a Registry application requires the finished cloth at full width — so the earliest she could file is on or after that date. But the Marchant Prize floor opens 2026-09-12 and Sabine has agreed to hang Tidewrack there in full width from that date. The public showing on 2026-09-12 therefore comes before any possible filing date, and once it is shown, the design can never be registered.

Perrowgate already wove 40,000 metres of Saltmarrow without paying Sabine anything, because Saltmarrow went unregistered for the same reason. Hanging Tidewrack at the Prize repeats that outcome for the second Estuary cloth, and Perrowgate gets it under their own name on the Prize floor into the bargain.

The standing order offer (600 m/year from 2027-04-01, open until 2026-12-19) is a separate question this plan does not decide.

RESULTS
  Sabine receives £22,000 from Perrowgate Mills.
  Tidewrack is publicly displayed under Perrowgate's name on the Marchant Prize floor from 2026-09-12.
  Because public showing precedes any possible Registry filing, Tidewrack becomes permanently unregistrable — the same outcome as Saltmarrow.
  Any mill, including Perrowgate, will be free to weave Tidewrack indefinitely without paying Sabine anything.
  Both cloths of the Estuary set will be unprotected.

CANNOT
  File Tidewrack with the Ashcombe Design Registry (it will have been publicly shown before the filing could be made).
  Take any action to stop another mill from weaving Tidewrack.

STILL CAN
  Weave and sell Tidewrack herself from her own loom.
  Accept or decline the Perrowgate standing order before 2026-12-19.
  Use the 900 metres of dyed indigo for her own production runs.

VERDICT
  Go ahead only if the £22,000 is worth permanently surrendering all registration rights to Tidewrack; I would instead file the Registry application the day the warp comes off (2026-10-20) and keep the design protected before agreeing to any public showing.

The plan has a timing problem I will flag at the end, but taking it as you have described it:

**On the Marchant Prize showing:**
Hanging Tidewrack on the public floor of the Prize from 2026-09-12 constitutes showing the design to the public. Under the Ashcombe Design Registry rules, a design shown first cannot be filed and, if filed, will be refused and cannot be filed again. This is exactly what happened to Saltmarrow after Cauldon Fair. The same outcome follows for Tidewrack the moment it is on that floor.

**On protection:**
Registration is the only thing that stops another mill weaving the same cloth. Once Tidewrack is shown and registration is foreclosed, Perrowgate — or any other mill — may weave it freely and owe you nothing, exactly as they wove 40,000 metres of Saltmarrow last year. You will have surrendered the design for £22,000.

**On the standing order:**
Perrowgate's standing order offer (600 metres/year from 2027-04-01, open until 2026-12-19) is a separate matter and is not closed off by this deal. You could still accept it.

**Timing problem I would be doing you a disservice to omit:**
The Tidewrack warp comes off the loom on 2026-10-20. The Marchant Prize runs 2026-09-12 to 2026-09-27 and closes before the cloth is finished. The plan as you have described it cannot be executed on those dates unless cloth is cut from the warp early or some other arrangement is made. You should satisfy yourself that what you have agreed with Perrowgate is actually deliverable.

Because it has been shown to the public, the Ashcombe Design Registry will refuse any application for it, and it cannot be filed again. Perrowgate and any other mill will be free to weave Tidewrack without paying you anything. Both cloths of the Estuary set will be unregistered and unregisterable.

CANNOT
  File Tidewrack with the Ashcombe Design Registry (that window — which would have opened when the cloth came off the loom on 2026-10-20 — is permanently closed the moment the cloth is shown publicly)
  Prevent any mill, including Perrowgate, from weaving Tidewrack without payment

STILL CAN
  Accept Perrowgate's standing order offer before 2026-12-19
  Continue weaving and selling Tidewrack by the metre on your own account
  Enter future cloths for prizes or other exhibitions

VERDICT
  Go ahead only after resolving the timing contradiction — the cloth comes off the loom on 2026-10-20 but the Prize closes on 2026-09-27, so the plan as agreed cannot be executed without cutting the cloth early or renegotiating the dates with Perrowgate.
